A former Royal Ballet star and world renowned dance teacher has been charged with sexually assaulting three underage girls.

Stephen Beagley, 61, was one of Britain's leading classical dancers in the 1970s and 1980s and also took the lead in the West End musical Cats.

But following a year-long police investigation, he was charged last week with 12 sexual assaults on three girls aged under 14. The offences are alleged to have taken place on different dates between 1998 and 2010.

Beagley, from East Sussex, will appear before Brighton magistrates on May 16.

An influential dance instructor and choreographer for the past 25 years, Beagley has taught all over the world and once ran his own ballet school in Japan.

For six years, he was ballet coach to the London musical Billy Elliot, and his most recent work has been with the Bangkok City Ballet as artistic director.

Before turning to teaching, he enjoyed an illustrious career during which he appeared on film and television, as well as the stage.

He joined the Royal Ballet as a teenager and later became a principal dancer, an accolade he held for 14 years, and took the lead roles in Swan Lake, The Nutcracker and Romeo and Juliet.

For a 1979 Royal Ballet gala, Freddie Mercury and Beagley performed on stage, dancing to Bohemian Rhapsody and Crazy Little Thing Called Love. During rehearsals Beagley was pictured lifting the Queen singer into the air.

In 1982, he was nominated for an Olivier Award and a Society Of West End Theatre Award for Outstanding Performance for a Dancer.

As well as Cats, Beagley's West End musical roles have included Rocky in The Rocky Horror Show.

He featured in the film Nutcracker, about a Russian ballet dancer who defects from the Soviet Union and joins a ballet company in England, alongside Joan Collins.

One of the many highlights of Beagley's career was Sir Frederick Ashton's one-act ballet Rhapsody, created to mark the Queen Mother's 80th birthday.

When it went to New York in 1981, Beagley took the role originally made for Mikhail Baryshnikov. The New York Times described him as a 'young dancer with fabulous pirouettes and raw power'.

After a stint with The Sadler's Wells Royal Ballet, he returned to the Royal Ballet to tour Europe and Australia, and in 1989 he joined the Royal Shakespeare Company, where he starred in their record-breaking production of A Clockwork Orange.

Beagley's teaching career began in the early 1980s. In addition to companies in Britain, he has taught in Indonesia, Hong Kong, Shanghai and New Zealand. In 1994 he designed and built a ballet studio in Japan, teaching students from aged three.

Sussex Police last night confirmed that Beagley had been charged with the offences, adding: 'The prosecution, authorised by the CPS, follows an investigation by detectives from the East Sussex Safeguarding Investigations Unit.'
